subject: general
question: Movement of fault lines can cause:
solution:
The correct answer is __**An Earthquake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **fault is a fracture or zone of fractures between two blocks of rock**. Faults allow the blocks to move relative to each other. This movement may occur rapidly, in the form of an earthquake 
 
• Earthquakes are usually caused when **underground rock suddenly breaks** and there is rapid motion along a fault. This sudden release of energy causes the seismic waves that make the ground shake.
 
• **Faults can be centimeters to thousands of kilometers long**. The fault surface can be vertical, horizontal, or at some angle to the surface of the earth. Faults can extend deep into the earth.
 
• Earthquakes recorded by seismographic networks are mapped and indicate the location of a fault.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91f1b714d837b4fc184ea927174e767064da91d9f8aa3415d97ed0e9b7c6d12f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Marcalli scale is used to measure the **intensity of an Earthquake**. Its range of intensity scale is from 1 - 12.
 
• Richter scale is used to measure the **magnitude scale of an earthquake**. Its measurements are denoted from 0 -10
 
• Richter Scale was developed by **Charles F. Richter in 1935**.
 
• Seismographs are instruments used to record seismic waves. Seismic waves are the **vibration from earthquake** that travel through the Earth.
